I am barely computer-literate enough to deploy crypto. I am not likely to author any original and effective crypto code any time soon. But until recently I had planned to set up a very open, very privacy-protecting system for anonymous speech. Ten years ago, I would have wanted such a system to be something very much like FreeNet, where any random person could surf in and post anonymous speech. The problem is that I don't want to be a party to human trafficking, so I want to design a system that would resist abuse by human traffickers. I think I know how to do it.

I don't particularly want to build a wonderful server that can be used by everyone around the world. I want to build a wonderful server that can be used by fewer than fifty people in my personal circle of acquaintances. That means I can design the system so that to use it, everyone has to show up to a location of my choosing, where I grant access to people whom I know by sight. They can play around with it for a while, and possibly they have persistent access once I have granted it. That system could be very anonymity-protecting. My friends could post silly memes without getting identified, and they could look over each other's shoulders and marvel at how easy it was to spot each other in person, but how hard it was to spot each other over the Internet.

Of course, this type of exercise is not scalable by me, and probably not scalable by most commercial Internet operators. In particular, it should resist most darknet market applications. Darknet buyers want to surf in anonymously. This would require physical access to the permission-granting person. However, even though my own personal instance of the code might be non-abusable, the source code might still be easy to abuse. If a criminal gang of traffickers were to get the source code, they might abuse it for communications among themselves.
